paras: The Toombsboro curfew shooting was an exchange of gunfire on the night of October 4–5, 1903, in Toombsboro, Wilkinson County, Georgia, between the town marshal, later joined by a posse, and a group of Black men he had ordered off a street corner under a new curfew ordinance. About 100 shots were reportedly fired without anyone being hit, and five Black men were jailed to be tried for assault with intent to murder.
Shortly before the shooting, the Toombsboro town council had passed an ordinance forbidding crowds from gathering on the streets after 9 o'clock at night.

On Sunday night, October 4, Marshal Rickerson found a number of Black men standing on a street corner and ordered them to disperse. According to the only account, the men instead drew pistols and fired at him, and he returned fire while retreating. Rickerson then gathered help and tried to arrest the men, and through the rest of the night and into Monday morning shots were exchanged between the group and the marshal's posse, an estimated 100 in all. None of the shots took effect.

Three of the men were arrested on Monday night and two more on Tuesday morning, and all five were taken to the jail at Irwinton to be tried for assault with intent to murder. None of the arrested men was named, and no report of their trial appears in the coverage.

The episode is known from a single item in the Savannah Morning News of October 8, a Dublin dispatch dated October 7 that passed on what several men from Wilkinson County had told in Dublin the day before. The paper headlined it "Riot at Toombsboro" with the deck "Shots Were Fired by Officers and by Negroes," though the text itself called it a "street fight" that was "bloodless" but "exciting." The dispatch gave the marshal's version as fact, including the claim that the Black men fired first, and treated the absence of casualties as a curiosity ("Strange to say").
No account from the arrested men or from the Black press was found, and the story ran in the same column as an unrelated Dublin item about an embezzlement case.

reader.title: Toombsboro curfew shooting
bases: A town marshal enforcing a curfew ordinance, and later a posse he gathered, fired on a group of Black men while trying to disperse and arrest them (A1).

The only report is one secondhand Dublin dispatch in the Savannah Morning News, relaying what 'several gentlemen from Wilkinson county' said (A1); no Black-press or second white-press report was found.

accounts.gist: The Black men drew pistols and fired when the marshal ordered them to disperse; he returned fire while retreating, then came back with a posse, and about 100 shots were exchanged overnight without anyone being hit.

framing.detail: Under the headline 'Riot at Toombsboro. Shots Were Fired by Officers and by Negroes,' the Savannah Morning News ran the visitors' version as fact, treating the bloodless exchange as a curiosity ('Strange to say').
